title: Local finite presentation is fppf local on the source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $(h_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $f$ is locally of finite presentation if and only if every $f\circ h_i$ is locally of finite presentation. Jointly surjective means every point of $X$ has a preimage in some $U_i$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian assumption is imposed; empty schemes and an empty covering family of the empty scheme are allowed.

proof.text: If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, then each $h_i$ has this property by hypothesis, so [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] applied to $h_i$ and $f$ proves that $f\circ h_i$ is locally of finite presentation. For the converse, assume this for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 036N, proof, composition condition; Morphisms Tag 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(x)\in V$, $x\in W$ and $W\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$. For each $i$, cover the open subset $h_i^{-1}(W)$ by affine opens $T_{i,\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{i,\alpha}$ of $U_i$ contained in $h_i^{-1}(W)$, using the same basis assertion. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], it suffices to show $R\to A$ is finitely presented for every such choice around $x$. If $X$ is empty there are no points to check and that definition already gives the result, including an empty covering family.

source.place: Tag 036N via Tag 036H (lemma-properties-morphisms-local-source), reduction to affine source and target; expanded as in Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] to $h_i$ and the affine pair $(T_{i,\alpha},W)$ to obtain flatness of $A\to B_{i,\alpha}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to $h_i$ with this pair and to $f\circ h_i$ with the pair $(T_{i,\alpha},V)$. Thus $A\to B_{i,\alpha}$ and $R\to B_{i,\alpha}$ are finitely presented. These are compatible ring towers $R\to A\to B_{i,\alpha}$ because the second scheme morphism is the composite $f\circ h_i$.

source.place: Tag 036N, affine condition (4), with Morphisms Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize) and 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize).

proof.text: Each $h_i$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Hence the subsets $h_i(T_{i,\alpha})$ are open in $X$ and contained in $W$. Joint surjectivity and the affine covers of $h_i^{-1}(W)$ imply that these images cover $W$: lift any $w\in W$ to some $u\in U_i$ and choose $T_{i,\alpha}$ containing $u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $W$ is quasi-compact. Choose finitely many pairs $(i_j,\alpha_j)$ whose images cover $W$, and write $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ for the selected affine opens. Only $W$ is required to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 036H, affine refinement of an fppf family; Tag 02KL, proof, open images and finite affine selection; Morphisms Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open).

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to form $Z=\coprod_j T_j$ and the maps $q:Z\to W$ and $p:Z\to V$ induced by the component maps. Uniqueness in the coproduct universal property gives $p=(f|_W)\circ q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\prod_jB_j$ and the specified component projections. The component images in $Z$ are open and closed and cover $Z$. The selected image covering of $W$ says exactly that $q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, replacement by the finite affine coproduct, supplying the refinement in Tag 036H; Schemes Tags 01JB and 01JC (disjoint gluing).

proof.text: At a point of the component $T_j\subseteq Z$, the local-ring map of $q$ is the local-ring map of the corresponding $h_{i_j}$, since source and target were restricted to open neighbourhoods. It is flat, so [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of $q$. The affine neighbourhood $T_j$ of that point has a finitely presented $A$-algebra by Step 3. With target $W$, this is exactly the pointwise definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] for $q$. The same neighbourhood has a finitely presented $R$-algebra by Step 3; with target $V$ it gives local finite presentation of $p$ by that definition.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, elementary justification of replacing the source by its selected disjoint affine opens; Morphisms Tags 01U3 and 01TP (definitions).

proof.text: All three schemes $Z,W,V$ are affine. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to their full affine opens gives that $A\to B$ is flat and finitely presented, and that $R\to B$ is finitely presented. Surjectivity of $q$ is precisely surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ under the affine identifications. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes $A\to B$ faithfully flat. The compatibility $p=(f|_W)q$ identifies $R\to B$ with the composite $R\to A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 036N, affine condition reduced to Tag 02KK; Algebra Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), flat and surjective on spectra implies faithfully flat.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-fppf-source-algebra] to $R\to A\to B$. Step 7 provides all three hypotheses: finite presentation of $R\to B$, faithful flatness of $A\to B$, and finite presentation of $A\to B$. Conclude that $R\to A$ is finitely presented. The neighbourhoods $x\in W$ and $f(x)\in V$ from Step 2 therefore witness finite presentation of $f$ at $x$ in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Since $x$ was arbitrary, $f$ is locally of finite presentation. This proves the converse.

source.place: Tag 036N, final sentence invoking Tag 02KK (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence-algebra); affine descent expanded as in Tag 02KL.

proof_origin.place: Tag 036N (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-fppf-local-source), expanding the affine-family reduction of Tag 036H by the finite affine selection in Tag 02KL and its algebra input Tag 02KK.
